8d5f16dc7592ba5fd72f806375b78739824cd2c8: A resort on a human scale, Jakobshorn (Davos) focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 41 km of runs are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially with family or for skiers who don't need to constantly renew their playground. Jakobshorn (Davos)'s family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for getting children started on skiing. With a summit at 2568 m and a village at 1535 m, snow reliability at Jakobshorn (Davos) is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can create tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. The budget for a stay at Jakobshorn (Davos) is clearly high: €91 for a day pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short, Jakobshorn (Davos) does not rival the giants of skiing and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
